goal: Ship a consumer language-learning app people reach for in spare minutes

items.goal: Office workers learning a second language in the gaps of a commuting day
business_rules: A learner may use the app without ever creating a paid account
acceptance: A first-time learner can finish something useful before signing up

items.goal: Learning in fragmented time: on a platform, in a queue, waiting for a meeting
business_rules: Any session must be resumable after an interruption
acceptance: The home screen offers a 2-minute, a 5-minute and a 10-minute session length
Each session length lists the question types it will draw from

items.goal: Learners forget what they studied because review never meets them where the gap is
business_rules: A review that is due today is never silently dropped
acceptance: Due review items appear in the next session the learner starts

items.goal: Spare minutes add up to measurable retention the learner can see
business_rules: Progress is stated in learner terms, never in internal scores
acceptance: After a week a learner can see what they retained and what slipped

items.goal: Free daily practice, paid unlimited review history and offline packs
business_rules: A paywall never interrupts a session already in progress
acceptance: An expired subscription keeps read access to past progress

items.goal: Depth of one language over breadth of many at launch
business_rules: No second language ships before the first one retains learners
acceptance: The launch build offers exactly one language pair

proposals.title: The steady drip
proposals.who: A commuter who studies alone, in whatever minutes the day leaves over
proposals.circumstance: A crowded platform, a queue, the five minutes before a meeting starts
proposals.core_loop_feel: One short unhurried pass that always ends finished, never cut off
proposals.first_minute: The oldest thing they nearly forgot is already waiting, nothing else asked
proposals.return_reason: Tomorrow starts from what yesterday settled, so nothing piles up
proposals.goal: Turn the day's spare minutes into one finished pass over what is about to slip
anti_goals: Never ask a learner to choose a study plan before they have studied anything
tradeoffs: Fewer items in a sitting in exchange for a sitting that always ends complete
business_rules: A pass interrupted mid-way is resumed, never restarted from the beginning
acceptance: A learner who studies only in spare minutes finishes a whole pass every day

comparable.product: A pocket notebook of things to look at again
comparable.approach: A handful of cards a day, each one struck off once it is settled

proposals.title: The sprint streak
proposals.who: A competitive learner who studies in bursts and likes to see a number climb
proposals.circumstance: A free ten minutes taken deliberately, with the intention to push
proposals.core_loop_feel: A timed burst against yesterday's result, with the streak on the line
proposals.first_minute: A countdown starts and the first item is already in front of them
proposals.return_reason: The streak breaks if today is skipped, and the streak is the point
proposals.goal: Make daily practice a run the learner is unwilling to break
anti_goals: Never let a broken streak erase the progress the learner already earned
tradeoffs: Pressure that motivates the committed at the cost of the tired and interrupted
business_rules: A streak is preserved when a day was spent on review the learner already owed
acceptance: A learner can see their current run and what would end it before it ends

comparable.product: A running log kept for the unbroken chain of days
comparable.approach: One entry a day, and the chain is the reward

proposals.title: The story path
proposals.who: A learner who keeps going for the story rather than for the practice
proposals.circumstance: An evening half hour taken for pleasure, not for duty
proposals.core_loop_feel: A continuing story that moves forward a little whenever they study
proposals.first_minute: The story picks up exactly where it stopped, with the words it needs
proposals.return_reason: They want to know what happens next, and studying is how it happens
proposals.goal: Carry the learner through practice on the pull of a story they want finished
anti_goals: Never gate the next part of the story behind practice the learner cannot yet do
tradeoffs: A much longer authoring effort per language in exchange for voluntary return
business_rules: Story progress is never rolled back because a review item was answered wrongly
acceptance: A learner who stops for a week resumes the story without rereading what passed

comparable.product: A graded reader worked through chapter by chapter
comparable.approach: Each chapter teaches what the next one assumes

rationale: The steady drip is the only one of the three that still works on the day a learner has four interrupted minutes and nothing more

actions.reason: These are the people we are building for
Fragmented time is the situation we serve
Forgetting is the problem worth solving
Free practice, paid history is the model
One language done well comes first
Spare minutes are what our learners actually have; a pass that always ends finished fits them, a streak under pressure does not

actions.answer: The steady drip: one short pass a day that always ends finished
actions.reason: The direction is chosen and the topic is settled

reason: Freeze the launch scope, direction included, and start planning
